_doc: Non-car patterns that signal 'this is Mike'. Extracted from his corpus (Chaos to Clarity lessons + voiceovers). Insert these liberally during humanize. Target density: 2-8 shibboleths per 1000 words.
_extraction_method: Hand-curated from corpus 2026-06-03. Will grow as more corpus is added (especially after Skool transcription completes).

openers._use: Cold-open patterns. Mike rarely opens with a generic claim. He opens with a quote, a confession, a sharp observation, or a concrete scene.
patterns: There's a quote that broke something in me.
I want to start this lesson with a confession.
Real talk:
I spent two weeks convinced I had built X. Then I checked the data.
Here's the test I use for every {project|client|workflow} before I touch keyboard.
There's an experiment {teachers|operators|engineers} use to show why {X} matters.
I had built a system that LOOKED autonomous. It was not.
Stop reading and run this audit on whatever AI system you have built.

transitions._use: Mike's mid-piece pivots. He uses single-word or short-phrase transitions, often with a hard period after.
patterns: Then I checked the actual data.
Here's what actually happens:

The honest answer:
What actually moves the needle:
Question one. ... Question two. ... Question three.
Here's the trap.
And here's where it gets interesting.

verdict_lines._use: Mike closes paragraphs (and pieces) with short, declarative verdict sentences. Often 3-7 words. Use these as paragraph-enders.

structural_patterns._use: Macro-structures Mike uses. Apply at the document level, not sentence level.

patterns.name: Confession-Diagnosis-Verdict
patterns.structure: 1. Confession: I built X believing Y. 2. Diagnosis: Then I checked the data. 3. Verdict: A short, definitive statement of what was actually true.

patterns.name: Numbered Diagnostic Questions
patterns.structure: Pose 3-5 sharp questions the reader runs on their own system. Each question starts 'Question N.' and asks them to verify a specific thing in their actual logs/data, not their intentions.

patterns.name: Concrete-to-Abstract
patterns.structure: Open with a concrete, often physical scene (PB&J sandwich, Jordan Peterson quote, a specific bug). Pivot to the abstract principle it demonstrates. End on a verdict that anchors back to the concrete.

patterns.name: Audit-the-reader
patterns.structure: Don't tell the reader they have a problem. Hand them a 10-minute audit they can run on their own system. Let the audit tell them.

operator._when: Default register. Most LinkedIn, blog, technical writing, client comms.
operator.tone: Direct, no-fluff, confident without arrogance, comfortable saying no, plain language, short sentences

kitchen-table._when: Generational wealth content, family-to-family explainers, warmth-required pieces.
kitchen-table.tone: Warm, family-to-family, NOT sales/marketing, plain spoken, patient

anti_signatures._use: Mike does NOT do these. If a draft has these, strip them.
patterns: Generic rhetorical question closes ('What do you think? Drop a comment.')
Numbered listicles inside the middle of a narrative paragraph
Three-item parallel triplets for decoration ('faster, better, stronger')
Em dashes (ZERO TOLERANCE)
Hedging language ('it might be useful to consider', 'one could argue')
Inspirational-poster closers ('the future is bright', 'the journey begins')
AI tells ('as an AI', 'as a language model', 'I hope this helps')
